title: Liver biopsy and acute hepatology in intensive care unit patients
one_line_summary: Liver biopsy in **critically** ill ICU patients provides decisive diagnostic and prognostic value for primary liver diseases when non-invasive workups are inconclusive, with transjugular and mini-laparoscopic approaches offering favorable safety profiles.
key_pearls: - **Transjugular liver biopsy (TJLB)** is the preferred tissue sampling technique in **critically** ill ICU patients with coagulopathy or ascites due to lower procedure-related bleeding risks compared to percutaneous approaches.

- In **acute liver failure (ALF)**, histological examination is specifically **recommended** in cases of unknown etiology, suspected **acute severe autoimmune hepatitis (AS-AIH)**, or suspected malignant infiltration.

- Extent of parenchymal necrosis on histology provides prognostic utility in **ALF**: a threshold of **>75%** hepatocellular necrosis correlates with poor transplant-free **survival** and **mortality** rates ranging from **60% to 100%**.

- For **acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF)**, biopsy should be reserved for identifying actionable or rare intrahepatic precipitants, such as **AIH** flares, unclear **drug-induced liver injury (DILI)**, or **alcohol-associated hepatitis (AAH)** with an inconclusive clinical history.

- Secondary liver injuries, such as **septic cholestasis** and **hypoxic hepatitis**, are common in the ICU but generally do not warrant liver biopsy as histopathology is non-specific and does not change therapeutic management.
- Adequate histopathological evaluation requires tissue cylinders of **15–20 mm** in length obtained with a **16 G** needle containing **>10 portal fields** (minimum **>5 portal fields**).
population: Critically ill intensive care unit (ICU) patients presenting with severe liver dysfunction, acute liver failure (ALF), or acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF).

sections.heading: Introduction and Differentiation of ICU-Related Liver Dysfunction
sections.content:
- Hepatic impairment occurs in up to **70%** of ICU patients and **significantly** impacts **mortality** depending on the underlying cause.
- **Sepsis-induced cholestasis** is driven by cytokine-mediated down-regulation of hepatocellular transport proteins (e.g., **NTCP**, **MRP 2–4**) induced by endotoxins such as **LPS**; liver biopsy shows unspecific portal inflammation, centrilobular necrosis, and ductular cholestasis and is not **recommended**.
- **Hypoxic hepatitis** (*'shock liver'*) is defined by: 1) appropriate clinical setting, 2) **AST** and **ALT** elevation **≥20x upper limit of normal** (or **AST ≥5x** in some criteria), and 3) exclusion of primary acute liver disease.
- Histopathology in hypoxic hepatitis demonstrates centrilobular necrosis and sinusoidal congestion, but biopsy is generally not indicated unless liver dysfunction persists after resolving the systemic event.
- Primary hepatic entities (**ALF**, **ACLF**) account for approximately **1%** of ICU admissions, whereas secondary liver involvement (**septic cholestasis**, **hypoxic hepatitis**) affects up to **20%** and **4%** of ICU patients, respectively.
section_pearls: Distinguish primary liver disease from secondary ICU liver injury early to avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

sections.heading: Role of Liver Biopsy in Specific Primary Liver Diseases
sections.content:
- **Acute Liver Failure (ALF)**:
  - Defined by coagulopathy (**INR >1.5**), hepatic encephalopathy without prior liver disease, elevated bilirubin/enzymes, and symptom onset **≤26 weeks**.
  - Biopsy is indicated for: indeterminate etiology, suspected **AS-AIH** (IgG, **ANA**, **SMA** ambiguous), and history of malignancy.
  - Severe **AS-AIH** accounts for **3–6%** of ALF cases; biopsy confirms interface hepatitis and rules out overlapping syndromes or pre-existing cirrhosis (present in **25–30%** at presentation).
  - **Corticosteroid** therapy should not be delayed for biopsy execution in suspected **AS-AIH**.
  - **>75%** parenchymal necrosis predicts transplant-free **mortality** of **60–100%** and can guide liver transplantation listing.
- **Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF)**:
  - Defined by acute decompensation of underlying cirrhosis with extrahepatic organ failure and severe systemic inflammation.
  - Biopsy is used selectively to identify specific precipitating triggers: **AIH** flares, **DILI**, **AAH** with uncertain anamnesis, **Wilson disease**, or **visceral leishmaniasis**.
  - Biopsy in high-grade **ACLF** (**ACLF grade 3**) due to **AAH** has limited utility if used solely to justify **corticosteroid** therapy, as steroid response is only **8%** in **ACLF 3** with a high risk of infectious complications.
  - **Wilson disease** in the acute setting shows **ALP-to-total bilirubin ratio <4** and **AST-to-ALT ratio >2.2** (sensitivity and specificity **>90%**); tissue copper quantification via biopsy (*Leipzig criteria*) aids indeterminate cases.
section_pearls: Parenchymal necrosis >75% in ALF strongly indicates poor transplant-free survival.
In ACLF 3 from AAH, corticosteroid response is only 8% and carries high infection risks.

sections.heading: Post-Transplantation and Donor Evaluation Considerations
sections.content:
- Persistent liver enzyme elevation **>48 hours** post-liver transplantation with ALF signs indicates primary graft non-function, warranting biopsy to rule out vascular/surgical complications versus severe ischemia-reperfusion injury.
- Liver injury persisting **>1 week** post-transplantation strongly suggests **acute cellular rejection (ACR)**; biopsy is **mandatory** to confirm **ACR** prior to escalating immunosuppressive therapy.
- Pre-procurement bedside liver biopsy is indicated in deceased organ donors with extended criteria (age **>60 years**, **BMI >35 kg/m2**, alcohol history, viral hepatitis serology, or abnormal liver enzymes) to assess steatosis and graft suitability.
section_pearls: Biopsy is required to confirm acute cellular rejection before escalating post-transplant immunosuppression.

sections.heading: Technical Approaches and Procedural Bleeding Risks
sections.content:
- **Transjugular Liver Biopsy (TJLB)**:
  - Preferred first-line technique in **critically** ill patients with severe coagulopathy (**INR >1.5–3.0**), thrombocytopenia (**platelets <50 x10^3/uL**), or refractory ascites.
  - Allows concurrent hepatic venous pressure gradient (**HVPG**) measurement.
  - Non-**inferior** tissue diagnostic yield compared to percutaneous approaches, with reduced bleeding/hematoma rates.
- **Percutaneous Liver Biopsy (PLB)**:
  - Standard bedside approach; requires ultrasound assistance/guidance.
  - Provides larger, less fragmented tissue cylinders but carries increased bleeding risk in severe coagulopathy (**INR >1.8–2.0**, **platelets <20–25 x10^3/uL**, **fibrinogen <100 mg/dL**).
  - **Contraindicated** in obstructive cholestasis, severe intrahepatic/biliary infections, and uncorrected severe coagulopathy.
- **Mini-Laparoscopic Liver Biopsy (mLLB)**:
  - Viable alternative when TJLB is technically unfeasible or when direct visual inspection of peritoneum/focal lesions and local surface hemostasis are required.
  - Can be performed at ICU bedside under conscious sedation and local anesthesia.
- **Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Liver Biopsy (EUSLB)**:
  - Feasible for left liver lobe sampling or combined endoscopic indications; currently lacks dedicated validation studies in **critically** ill ICU cohorts.
section_pearls: TJLB enables simultaneous HVPG measurement and minimizes capsular bleeding risks in coagulopathic ICU patients.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Comprehensive synthesis of international guideline recommendations (**EASL**, **AASLD**) integrated with real-world clinical experience from a major European tertiary liver center; detailed technical comparison of four liver biopsy modalities in **critical** care settings.
- **Limitations**: Sparse prospective evidence and randomized controlled trials evaluating liver biopsy directly within ICU populations; lack of unified international consensus regarding bleeding risk stratification thresholds in **critically** ill patients with liver failure.

drugs_doses.dose: Dose variable according to specific protocol
drugs_doses.indication: Acute severe autoimmune hepatitis (AS-AIH) or severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AAH)
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: High risk of severe infectious and septic complications, especially in advanced acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF 3).
